description:
We are a team of curious and motivated individuals participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

Our goal is to explore real-world challenges, develop creative solutions, and use science and technology to make a difference.

We are particularly interested in Earth Science, space exploration, coding, and innovative ideas.

We value creativity, teamwork, open-mindedness, and learning from each other. We welcome people with different backgrounds, skills, and perspectives.
summary:
GeoNota turns NASA's view of Earth into music. We built a browser-based "jukebox" that sweeps a scanning cursor across global satellite maps from west to east, reading the planet in 24 columns and 6 latitude bands. Each color the scanner sees becomes a musical note in real time: cool colors (deep ocean, cold land) play low pitches, warm colors (deserts, hot surfaces) play high ones, so you literally hear the shape of our planet's data.

You can scan five real NASA Earth Information Center datasets (sea-surface temperature, land-surface temperature, chlorophyll, vegetation, and aerosols) as still frames or animated movies, then watch and listen as patterns like ocean currents and seasonal greening turn into evolving melodies. A separate menu also lets you "play" any of 176 countries, whose outlines are tinted by latitude.

GeoNota makes Earth science intuitive, accessible, and genuinely fun: data you can feel, not just read.
details:
What it does: GeoNota is a web app that converts NASA Earth observation maps into sound. A scanning cursor sweeps each global map from west to east. At every step it samples the image in a grid of 24 columns by 6 latitude bands, and each color it reads is mapped to a musical note that plays in real time. Cool colors like deep ocean and cold land produce low pitches; warm colors like deserts and hot surfaces produce high pitches. The result is an audible, moving portrait of the planet.

How it works: The app loads real imagery from the NASA Earth Information Center (sea-surface temperature, land-surface temperature, chlorophyll, vegetation, and aerosols), as either still frames or animated movies. A canvas reads the pixel data, a brightness-and-warmth formula turns each cell into a pitch and volume, and the Web Audio API synthesizes the tones live while a visual cursor shows exactly what is being "played." A separate menu lets users pick any of 176 countries, whose outlines are generated and tinted by latitude so each nation plays its own short melody.

Benefits and impact: Earth science data is usually read on charts. GeoNota lets people hear it instead, which makes patterns like ocean currents, seasonal greening, and temperature gradients intuitive and memorable. It is accessible (useful for low-vision users and for anyone who learns better by listening), runs entirely in a browser with no install, and turns public NASA datasets into something people want to explore.

Tools and technology: Built as a modern web application. It uses HTML canvas for pixel sampling, the Web Audio API for real-time sound synthesis, and publicly available NASA Earth Information Center imagery. Country outlines are rendered from open Natural Earth geographic data.

Creativity: GeoNota reframes satellite data as a playable instrument rather than a static visualization, combining data sonification, interactive visuals, and exploration of both global datasets and individual countries in one tool.
